skill.name: code-documentation-code-explain
skill.description: Explain complex code with clear walkthroughs, visual diagrams, examples, pitfalls, and learning paths for developers at different skill levels.
skill.summary: Turns complex code into clear explanations, diagrams, examples, and learning guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static matches were reviewed against the cited files. All findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, Python documentation examples, inline file paths, Mermaid diagrams, and one benign learning URL.

Line 145 is a Python string for a Mermaid class diagram fence. No shell invocation or dynamic execution is present.
Line 171 appends a Markdown closing fence to text returned by the example. It is not a backtick shell execution primitive.
Line 648 discusses the literal Python syntax `except:` in prose. The backticks are Markdown formatting and do not run commands.
Line 750 stores a Real Python tutorial URL as a suggested learning resource. It is not used for automatic network access or data transfer.
Line 107 describes generating a Mermaid diagram from user-provided code structure. It is educational analysis, not host or system reconnaissance.
Line 117 creates a diagram node identifier such as F0. It does not enumerate local files, processes, users, or system state.
Line 132 maps function names to diagram node identifiers within an example. This is code-flow visualization, not system reconnaissance.
Line 427 calls a sample age validation function with a constant value. It is an educational example and has no reconnaissance behavior.
Line 524 starts a Mermaid class diagram in documentation. It does not request or reveal system information.
Line 564 starts another Mermaid diagram block for a design-pattern explanation. It is static documentation content.
Line 797 lists Common Pitfalls as an output section. It does not inspect or enumerate the host environment.
Line 35 contains an inline Markdown file path to a local resource. Backticks are formatting only and do not execute anything.
Line 46 references the playbook path in inline Markdown. It is a resource pointer, not Ruby or shell execution.

content.value_statement: Complex code is hard to teach, review, and onboard. This skill turns code into clear walkthroughs, diagrams, examples, and learning paths.
actual_capabilities: Explains code purpose, control flow, dependencies, and complexity hotspots.
Creates Mermaid flow diagrams and class diagrams for supported explanations.
Breaks algorithms into progressive steps with plain-language reasoning.
Generates interactive examples and practice exercises for learners.
Identifies pitfalls, edge cases, and safer implementation patterns.
Builds learning paths with topics, exercises, and suggested resources.
limitations: It explains existing code but does not implement refactors or new features.
It depends on the code and context supplied by the user.
Generated diagrams may need review for very large or dynamic systems.
External learning links are suggestions, not verified endorsements.

use_cases.title: Onboard New Engineers
use_cases.description: Create clear subsystem walkthroughs with concepts, diagrams, pitfalls, and practice tasks.

use_cases.title: Understand Legacy Code
use_cases.description: Turn unfamiliar modules into step-by-step explanations that show flow, dependencies, and risks.

use_cases.title: Create Learning Materials
use_cases.description: Draft tutorials, examples, and exercises that teach patterns and algorithms from real code.

prompt_templates.title: Explain A Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the selected code for a junior developer. Start with purpose, then describe inputs, outputs, flow, and common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Walk Through A Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step walkthrough for this module. Include key concepts, dependency flow, edge cases, and one practice exercise.

prompt_templates.title: Visualize An Algorithm
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this algorithm with a Mermaid flow diagram, a plain-language trace, complexity notes, and testing ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Build An Onboarding Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an onboarding guide for this subsystem. Include architecture overview, component responsibilities, sequence diagram, risky assumptions, and next learning tasks.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how a validation module works.
output: A purpose summary of the validation flow.
A step-by-step explanation of each decision point.
A list of edge cases and safer error-handling patterns.

output_examples.input: A team needs onboarding notes for a service component.
output: A diagram description showing major components and calls.
Practice tasks that help new engineers confirm understanding.

output_examples.input: A learner asks why a recursive algorithm is difficult.
output: A plain-language explanation of the base case and recursive step.
A call-stack walkthrough for one sample input.
Common mistakes and test cases to reinforce the concept.

best_practices: Provide the relevant code, surrounding files, and the learner skill level.
Ask for diagrams only when visual structure will improve understanding.
Review generated examples before using them in official documentation.
anti_patterns: Using the skill when the real task is to change code behavior.
Requesting broad codebase explanations without naming the target module.
Publishing generated diagrams without checking names, flows, and edge cases.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on explanation, teaching material, diagrams, examples, and learning guidance.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes Mermaid flow diagrams, class diagrams, and sequence-style explanations.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No. It can explain supplied code locally. One optional learning URL appears in the playbook.

faq.question: Can it explain large codebases?
faq.answer: Yes, but results are better when users provide a specific module, flow, or concept.

faq.question: Does it replace formal documentation?
faq.answer: No. It helps draft learning material that teams should review before publishing.
